title: A non-destructive DNA sampling technique for herbarium specimens
author: Lara Shepherd
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.i3jcgkn

steps.title: Prepare Staedtler Eraser
steps.instruction: Cut a Staedtler 'Mars Plastic' eraser into 2 pieces, each approximately 7mm in size, using a sterile razor blade.

steps.title: Sample Herbarium Specimen
steps.instruction: Rub a new piece of eraser across the leaf surface or petiole of each herbarium specimen, collect the resulting eraser fragments (erdu) onto a new piece of paper, and place them into a sterile 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube. Change gloves between each sample.

steps.title: Perform DNA Extraction
steps.instruction: Incubate the eraser fragments in Buffer ATL and proteinase-K on a heating block at 50°C for 3 hours. Then, follow the DNeasy blood and tissue kit instructions, using a final elution of 35 µl of Buffer AE, which can be spun through the column twice. Include negative extraction controls to monitor for reagent contamination.
